Prevention: Use certified weed-free seeds, clean farm machinery tools after working in an infested area, especially if you do not have the weed already on your land
Use water free from the seeds for irrigation to prevent introduction
Fallow land for at least one rice growing season, for ca. 4 months
Use crop rotation with upland crops every year, if possible
Flood the fields at least 10cm deep for 1 or 2 weeks after emergence of the weed and prior to planting
Monitoring: Annual or short-lived perennial, tufted grass (0.3-1.2 m high) with fibrous roots, sometimes with stolons.
Inflorescence erect, with numerous branches that point slightly upwards (each 2-13 cm long).
Look for emerging plants weekly after sowing - take direct control measures when the weed is found
Look for infestations along irrigation channels and take direct control actions when found
Direct Control: Hand pulling and hand hoeing during the croping cycle can be very effective
Animal pulled inter cultivation can dislodge weeds
Remove uprooted weeds from the field to prevent re- establishement
Undertake top weeding before the inflorescences of the weeds are matured to prevent seed set
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
